doc.title: Håkan Rydin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Glasgow, Scotland, July 27, 2016

title: How he composes: ideas, editing, finishing a new song
summary: Rydin describes composing from an idea, completing and rewriting a song he premiered the day before.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well let’s suppose I had a budget to commission you to write a new piece for a quartet.
How do you go about that? Is there a composing process that you do?

Well first I would ask about the deadline. Because — not what we would work for. I think almost every composer, arranger, they end up the last day. I don’t think I have a very good answer to that question. I am not that kind of guy who can sit down at 10 o’clock and write a song and write from 10 until 12, as some professional composers do. So I haven’t written that many, but I have written all over the years, and I have a couple of songs that I’m happy with. And it’s often from an idea. You get an idea — you get it anytime, anywhere. And it can be a melody, it can be a chord progression, it can be a rhythm, it can be a character or something. You get an idea and then you work it out. And if it’s — often the best songs are quickly written, but you can always edit. You might notice, I played a new song yesterday, and I wrote it I think about a month ago. And it was like that. I got an idea. I got it almost ready, but the last four bars I had trouble with. So I’ve learned that you should always complete it. Because always I have lots of ideas that are not completed. So I completed it. And I wasn’t happy with it. I rewrote it after a week, I rewrote it three times until I just found out — and then I had to change it. So I will not change it now. But it took some time. But in your own music you are free to edit it if you get a better idea. And it could be sometimes very small things. In this case it was pretty small things. I just found out that it was easier to have another section to do the improvisation, because the melody was pretty long and it was too long to improvise it. So I took parts of it to improvise on. For example, I did a little edit on the edit. I found a new ending.
Sometimes it’s hard to know when to stop something.
